newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW - Morgan Stanley bullish on Mexican stocks.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Morgan Stanley bullish on Mexican stocks.

text.p: U.S. brokerage Morgan Stanley thinks now is the time to buy Mexican stocks -- before everyone else does.
Mexican stock prices are cheap and poised to benefit next year from a growing domestic economy, according to Robert Pelosky, Morgan Stanley's head of Latin America strategy.
"We see the market in U.S. dollar terms growing about 20 percent next year," Pelosky told Reuters during an interview Thursday in Mexico City.
U.S. interest rates are likely to rise next year and could draw money away from Latin American stock markets, Pelosky said.

But local interest rates are a more important measure of stock market performance, he said, adding that local rates in Mexico are still likely to fall as inflation wanes, narrowing spreads with U.S. Treasuries and lifting stock prices.

"We see about a 700 basis point drop in local interest rates in Mexico over the next 12 months. That's all we need to see," Pelosky said separately during an address to a Mexico City conference on global investment management.
He added that a sluggish U.S. stock market next year may finally attract investors not dedicated to emerging markets in search of higher returns.
"We think weakness in U.S. stocks in 1997 will help Latin American markets, not hurt," he told Reuters.

Mexico surprised foreign investors this year with its quick return to international debt markets after its peso woes in 1994-95. Prices on its Brady bonds have surged and spreads between its sovereign debt and Treasuries have narrowed.
"1996 was the year of debt; it was a transition. 1997 is really going to be the year of equity," Pelosky said.
